subject: Request: fine-grain data-use exception for embedded analytics (DPA redline)
messages:
From: Rita Gomez <rita@storelytics.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Request: embedded analytics telemetry carveout — DPA redline

Ava,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. Per our legal team's review, we've attached an annotated DPA with a narrow exception request so Storelytics can receive aggregated telemetry for the "embedded analytics" dashboard we're integrating into Acme's product. Key points in the redline: 

- Purpose: aggregated/anonymous metrics only (counts, histograms, top-N queries).
- Identifiers: hashed non-PII identifiers only (customer_id hashed + HMAC). No raw request text or KV cache dumps.
- Retention: 90 days for aggregated records (we noted a 90d retention clause).
- Subprocessor: allow Storelytics as a subprocessor for this specific, limited endpoint.
- Security controls requested: salted hashing, KMS-managed salt rotation, and ability to audit the hashing process.

We're requesting sign-off from Product (feasibility/implementation delta) and Security (controls and threat model) by COB Dec 6 so we can proceed with the integration schedule. I've attached the redline and included a short summary of the changes at the top of the doc.

Attachments: Storelytics_DPA_redline_20261129.docx (annotated)

Can you confirm who on your side should own the implementation plan and who will be the contact for the security audit/demo?

Appreciate it —
Rita Gomez
Head of Partnerships, Storelytics
rita@storelytics.com
[Attachment: Storelytics_DPA_redline_20261129.docx]

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T10:05:00-05:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: embedded analytics telemetry carveout — DPA redline

Folks — forwarding Storelytics' redline. High level asks from external (summarized): aggregated metrics only, hashed non-PII ids, 90d retention, Storelytics as a narrow subprocessor for the aggregation endpoint.

Product ask: can we implement runtime hashing + HMAC (salt in KMS) and guarantee that no request-level PII or KV cache is exported? If this requires changes to the runtime, please call out timeline and perf impact. Also confirm whether we can gate this behind a feature flag + sampling.

Security ask: do the proposed controls (salted HMAC in KMS, rotation, audit log) meet our bar to allow a subprocessor? If you need architecture/diagram we'll get one from infra.

I've attached the redline and added HubSpot deal id DL-75431. Want to respond to Storelytics with a list of required changes and whether Security can provisionally sign off. Can you reply with clear owners/timelines? Targeting Dec 6 sign-off.

Thanks —
Ava Chen
Senior Strategic Partnerships, Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.com
[Forwarded attachment: Storelytics_DPA_redline_20261129.docx]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T11:18:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: embedded analytics telemetry carveout — DPA redline

Thanks for the ping, Ava. I reviewed the redline and scribbled a recommended implementation approach. Quick summary: 

- Feasibility: Yes, we can support aggregated telemetry for embedded analytics without exporting request-level tokens or KV cache contents. We'll need to add a runtime telemetry pipeline that performs: (1) selective accept filters (only aggregation metrics), (2) hashing+HMAC of any identifier fields before any downstream export, and (3) metadata-only payloads (counts/top-n).
- Perf: adding the per-request hashing path will add ~20–35ms P95 on the request path if done synchronously. We can avoid tail impact by doing asynchronous aggregation for most customers and sampling at 10% for live traffic.
- Feature gating: we should implement a per-customer feature flag plus a sampling policy. That lets us enable Storelytics for the Acme pilot and iterate.
- Data model changes needed in the redline: explicitly prohibit export of KV-cache snapshots, request text, and un-hashed identifiers.
- Retention: product prefers 30d for aggregated metrics to reduce cost; legal asked 90d. If Security is comfortable with KMS rotation and limited access, we can accept 90d for the pilot but prefer 30d as default.

Action items (proposed):
1) Product (me) will create a dev spike (JIRA-1123) to prototype runtime hashing + sampling (ETA: 3 weeks).
2) Infra/SRE to produce a simple diagram of the telemetry path and where hashing happens (owner: infra, please assign).
3) Security to provide gating checklist for conditional subprocessor approval.
4) Legal to redline wording to specify endpoint and retention.

If Security is comfortable with KMS-managed salts and an audit demo, Product can commit to a pilot timeline. I can draft the short technical appendix Storelytics needs to sign.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Product, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
[Related: JIRA-1123, https://drive.redwood.example/drive/folders/1a2b3c/embedded-analytics-spec]

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:06:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: embedded analytics telemetry carveout — DPA redline

Thanks — I looked through Storelytics' requested redline and Karthik's notes. Security is prepared to grant a conditional approval for the subprocessor exception subject to the following hard requirements: 

1) Runtime masking: identifiers must be transformed with an HMAC using a customer-specific salt stored in KMS (no local plaintext salts). Salt rotation policy documented and enabled.
2) No raw request or KV-cache exports: the redline must explicitly prohibit export of request text, raw tokens, and KV cache dumps.
3) Dedicated subproc path: exports to Storelytics must go through a dedicated, audited subprocessor pipeline (VPC peering or private egress) with mutual TLS and signed ingestion.
4) Audit demo: Schedule a security audit demo (30–45 mins) where infra demonstrates masking, salt rotation, and that raw logs are inaccessible to Storelytics. We will not finalize approval until we observe the demo.
5) Access controls: RBAC for the aggregation dataset, limited to a named Storelytics account and reviewed quarterly.

If Product implements the approach Karthik outlined and Infra produces the small architecture diagram + threat model, Security can sign off for the pilot (90d retention may be allowed for pilot only; long-term we want 30d default). Please circulate an updated redline with the explicit prohibitions and the subprocessor scope limited to the aggregation endpoint.

Attaching a quick sketch of the expected runtime masking flow for reference.

Olga Petrov
Director, Security Engineering
olga_petrov@redwood.com
[Attachment: psm_runtime_masking_diagram.png]
